title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $9.03 show median 8.5 vs baseline 7.7, but no uplift. Past $9.03 week (2026-09-28) had no lift. A 2.3% increase likely dampens demand, especially with no promotion.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. This may lead to stockouts or reduced availability, lowering actual demand. No historical data on this exact issue, but plausible.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.7. No events or promotions are planned. The price increased 2.3% to $9.03, which is above regular price. Recent weeks at $9.03 show weak sales (median 8.5, vs baseline 7.7), but no clear lift. The past promotion at $9.03 (2026-09-28) had no uplift (x1.00), and the only deep discount (30% off) had a strong lift (x2.86), but that was not at current price. The supplier warning of short delivery introduces supply risk, likely reducing demand. No seasonal or event drivers apply. The classical model suggests no uplift, which aligns with weak evidence. The price increase and supply risk both suggest downward pressure. Evidence is thin for price effect (only 2 data points). Confidence is low.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.7 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 33.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 21.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
